meta: Dramas like Life on Mars: six cold, careful crime dramas that trust you to sit with an unanswered question.
standfirst: A modern profiler wakes up in 1988 with no forensics, a squad that solves cases with its fists, and a mystery about his own situation the show refuses to explain cleanly. The pull is the mix: proper period procedure, real ambiguity, and a lead who cannot tell whether any of it means anything. These six sit near that, and we say which ones give you an answer.

picks.why: The same coldness, held for sixteen episodes without blinking. A prosecutor who feels almost nothing works a corruption case with a detective who feels everything, and the script trusts you to follow a genuinely complicated conspiracy unaided. Same refusal to reward you with a tidy moral. Difference: no period setting and no fantasy premise, and the institution is the antagonist rather than the era.

Two eras, one case, rules that hold. A radio link across twenty years, cold cases reopened, and the tightest plotting on the site. Same idea that policing changes but the crimes do not. Difference: it commits fully to its mechanism where Life on Mars keeps its own deliberately unresolved, and it is far more emotional about the loss at the centre.

The exact mirror image. A 1986 detective chases a serial killer into 2017, which is this premise reversed, and the case work is patient and satisfying across sixteen episodes. Same interest in old policing as method. Difference: it is warm, it resolves everything, and the partnership becomes affectionate, none of which Life on Mars is willing to give you.

Period profiling, done as unglamorous work. Korea's first profiler in the 1990s, building a method from nothing while the institution resists him, and the interview sequences carry it. Same faith that procedure is enough tension. Difference: no genre device at all, and it is a much slower, flatter watch.

Ambiguity as the whole design. Two policemen each convinced the other is a murderer, and the show keeps that unresolved far longer than seems possible, with the best acting in this catalog. Same pleasure of never being sure what you are looking at. Difference: the setting is contemporary and small-town, and the answers do eventually arrive in full.

The same era-policing, played for entertainment. 1958 Seoul, a squad assembling fast, and a case-a-week rhythm with the period detail worn lightly. Same enjoyment of detectives who work without any modern tools. Difference: it is a comedy with a clean moral spine, so the dread and the ambiguity are entirely absent.

against.title: Good Boy
against.why: Same writer, and that is the whole basis for the recommendation. It is a broad action comedy about Olympic medallists joining the police, built on a repeating loop of fight, injury and recovery. Nothing in it wants the discomfort Life on Mars is made of.

against.title: Vagabond
against.why: Recommended as serious Korean crime with scale. It is a conspiracy action thriller with a body count and an ending that services a second season that never arrived. Procedure is not in it anywhere.

against.title: Voice
against.why: Suggested for the OCN thriller lineage. It goes at violence as spectacle, with a villain designed to be enjoyed, where Life on Mars keeps its crimes small, grubby and period-accurate.
